correctness.rationale: Total cover time equals the sum, over every deleted prefix, of the number of edges remaining uncovered. With remaining part counts \(r_i\) and fixed total \(R\), the remaining edge count is \((R^2-\sum_i r_i^2)/2\), so each prefix is optimized by maximizing the convex squared sum subject to the part capacities. Moving remaining mass from a smaller-capacity part toward a larger-capacity part never decreases that squared sum, proving that larger parts should remain full first. One smallest-part-first block ordering attains these prefix minima simultaneously. Summing the positions of the vertices in each exhausted block gives the displayed formula. The exhaustive verifier through order eight is a stress test only.

value.rationale: Complete multipartite graphs are the natural many-part extension of the previously solved complete-bipartite family. The theorem gives a transparent optimal structure and exact closed form for every number of parts, providing a useful dense-family benchmark for current MSVC work.
residual_risks: An obscure older cograph or ordering result may contain the same complete-multipartite formula under different terminology.

final_claim: For every finite complete multipartite graph with part sizes in nondecreasing order, minimum-sum vertex cover is attained by exhausting parts from smallest to largest, and the exact closed formula is the stated sum over block contributions; it strictly extends the known complete-bipartite formula.
limitations: Finite simple complete multipartite graphs only.
No analogous formula is claimed for multipartite graphs with missing cross-edges or arbitrary cographs.
